messages.author: 665b3d97beb30882
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] BIC to calculate summary statistics to compare models
parts:
Hi -- it is possible, but there is no function that does it at the moment.  But, the question for BIC is very simple, you could do in Excel, all you need is the ML log-likelihood and the number of free parameters.

There is a deep philosophical question about whether AIC or BIC is better. The short version, on my understanding, is:

1. AIC (or AICc for small datasets) represents the philosophy that the "real life model" is very complex, with many parameters -- perhaps an infinite number of parameters, or at least, way more parameters than you have in your model.  In this worldview, you never have the true model as one of your candidate models, you are just interested in which model(s) have a smaller distance to the truth, and you are just trying to find the main effects (parameters that greatly improve the likelihood).  This is what AIC measures.



2. BIC represents the philosophy that the true model is in the set of candidates, and that there is a limited number of free parameters in the true model.  There is nothing especially "Bayesian" about BIC, actually both AIC and BIC can be thought of as assuming different priors about what reality looks like.

BIC is probably more appropriate in cases where you have enough models/parameters that basically all different rates etc. are covered -- e.g. the case with time-reversible DNA models, where the complete model is GTR+G with every partition having a separate set of parameters and all of the other models are subsets of that.  In this sort of situation, BIC can help you pick a DNA partitioning scheme that avoids overfitting / achieve a better balance of model flexibility and having-enough-data-to-estimate-the-parameters in Bayesian MCMC.

(see publications by Burnham and Anderson for extensive discussion of AIC vs. BIC)

IMHO, in the current state of historical biogeography models, we are pretty clearly in situation #1, but everyone can make up their own mind about that.

Cheers!
Nick
